T: From the orphanage to the mansion, with dessert.
D: An orphan is invited to spend a week with billionaire Oliver Warbucks.
P: Serve the snacks when Annie arrives at the Warbucks mansion.
S: the good version, with brown sugar
Oats cooked slowly in milk with a pinch of salt, topped with brown sugar caramelised under the grill and a spoon of cream.
Creamy chicken and mushroom pastry cases, plus asparagus wrapped in prosciutto
Bake vol-au-vent cases crisp, fill with chicken and mushroom in a thyme cream sauce. Blanched asparagus spears wrapped in prosciutto alongside.
Stovetop popcorn popped in coconut oil, tossed in melted butter and salt
Pop kernels in coconut oil, toss with melted butter and fine salt while hot, serve in paper cones.
M: Whole chicken with tarragon butter under the skin, roasted golden
Dry-brine a chicken overnight, tarragon butter under the skin, roast at 220C for 20 minutes then 180C to 72C in the thigh. Pan gravy, roast potatoes and buttered peas.
Chicken thighs in a curry of onion, ginger, garlic, garam masala, tomato and yoghurt, simmered 30 minutes, basmati rice.
W: Vanilla ice cream under hot chocolate fudge sauce and whipped cream
Hot fudge of dark chocolate, cream and golden syrup poured over vanilla ice cream in tall glasses, whipped cream, toasted almonds and a cherry.
K: Mansion ginger beer and orange punch
Orange juice, lime, mint and ginger beer over ice, no alcohol

Spicy ginger beer with fresh orange juice, lime and mint, served from a punch bowl over plenty of ice. In a large jug, combine 400ml orange juice, 60ml lime juice and a handful of torn mint. Add ice, then pour in 800ml chilled ginger beer and stir gently. Add orange slices and serve in glasses with a mint sprig.

steps.text: Bake the vol-au-vent cases until crisp.
Dice the chicken and mushrooms and fry in butter until browned.
Add the cream and thyme and reduce until thick, then fill the cases.
Blanch the asparagus and wrap each spear in half a slice of prosciutto.
Heat the oil with three kernels in a covered pot.
When they pop, add the rest of the kernels, cover and shake until the popping slows.
Toss with the butter and salt, then fill paper cones.
The night before, salt the chicken and leave uncovered in the fridge.
Mix the softened butter with chopped tarragon and push it under the skin.
Roast at 220C with the halved potatoes.
Lower to 180C and roast until the thigh reads 72C.
Rest the chicken and make gravy from the pan juices and stock.
Cook the peas and toss with butter.
Melt the chocolate with the cream and golden syrup into a hot fudge.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan and whip the cream.
Scoop the ice cream into tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with whipped cream, almonds and a cherry.

s.note: Chicken and mushroom vol-au-vents with prosciutto asparagus
s.how: Bake 16 vol-au-vent cases until crisp. Fry 250g diced chicken thigh and 150g mushrooms, add 150ml cream and thyme and reduce. Fill the cases. Blanch 2 bunches asparagus and wrap each spear in half a slice of prosciutto.

s.note: Buttery salted popcorn in paper cones
s.how: Heat 2 tbsp coconut oil with 3 kernels, and when they pop add 120g kernels, cover and shake until the popping slows. Toss with 50g melted butter and fine salt while hot. Roll paper into cones and fill them up.

m.note: Tarragon butter roast chicken with gravy, potatoes and peas
m.how: Dry-brine a 1.8kg chicken overnight. Push 60g butter mixed with chopped tarragon under the skin. Roast at 220C for 20 minutes, then 180C until the thigh hits 72C, with 1kg potatoes. Make gravy with 250ml stock. Serve with buttered peas.

w.note: Hot fudge sundaes with cream, almonds and a cherry
w.how: Melt 150g dark chocolate with 150ml cream and 2 tbsp golden syrup into a hot fudge. Scoop vanilla ice cream into four tall glasses, pour over the fudge and top with whipped cream, toasted flaked almonds and a cherry.
